alloy.preparation: Fabricated from Ni 99.99%, Cr 99.99% and Mo 99.95% pieces by vacuum arc melting, with SEM checking/remelting as needed for homogeneous defect-free solid-solution ingots. Two-stage homogenization: 1204 °C for 24 h, then 1260 °C for 42 h, followed by water quenching. Small sections solder-connected in 1¼-inch multi-electrode mounts; Dexter Hysol EE4183/HD3561 epoxy at 100 g resin:12.5 g hardener, exposed areas 0.004–0.05 cm². Ground and polished to 1 µm diamond. If reused, repolished, low-viscosity Buehler Epo-thin (10 g resin:3.9 g hardener) filled prior crevices, cured overnight, reground/repolished to 1 µm. Individual first-use/reuse identities are not given.
alloy.microstructure: Solid-solution alloys; SEM used to verify homogeneous ingots, with remelting as necessary.

test_method.procedure_description: Scribner 910B multichannel microelectrode analyzer, three-electrode setup with SCE reference and graphite-rod counters; forward/reverse scans at 2 mV/s. Figure 3.9 panel-specific temperature retained. Instrument current limit 100 µA/channel creates vertical current-limit sections (0.001–0.1 A/cm² depending on area); this can affect pit size/number and repassivation. Starting potential and fixed reversal current are not independently specified.
test_method.pitting_criterion: Experimental Ep-exp from anodic-polarization datasets. Authors assign 600 mV to alloys lacking a distinct pitting potential before transpassivity; such values are transpassive-onset surrogates. Rapidly corroding alloys with no passive region are not automatically stable-pit thresholds; no universal numerical current criterion is specified.
